subject.title: Import Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter captures into the canonical local store

question: Should Birdclaw adopt third-party passive-capture files as a supported core ingestion source, and if so should the first contract be limited to Scrollmark canonical bundle v1?
rationale: The choice establishes a maintained external format contract and durable provenance, completeness, account-scoping, migration, and backup behavior that cannot be selected safely from implementation details alone.

options.title: Support Scrollmark v1 first
options.body: Approve a narrow core importer for the versioned Scrollmark canonical bundle, with explicit provenance and backup-compatible schema changes, while deferring legacy and twitter-web-exporter formats.

options.title: Support multiple producers now
options.body: Define a common capture-import abstraction and accept Scrollmark legacy shapes and twitter-web-exporter in the first release, accepting a larger compatibility and validation surface.

options.title: Defer passive-capture imports
options.body: Keep official archives, Birdclaw backups, and live transports as the only supported ingestion contracts until the provenance and completeness architecture is designed separately.

recommendation.title: Support Scrollmark v1 first
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow core importer for the versioned Scrollmark canonical bundle, with explicit provenance and backup-compatible schema changes, while deferring legacy and twitter-web-exporter formats.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository vision and archive-ingestion history make steipete the strongest available owner for the core format and persistence decision.
